newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS-UNITED FRONT TIES TO BE STABLE

Congress president Sitaram Kesri assured United Front (UF) convenor Chandrababu Naidu that his party would support the UF to form the next government. Claimimg the withdrawal of the Congress's letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma staking a claim to form the government as a formality, Kesri said this would be done as soon as the UF elected a new leader. Kesri was said to have also told Naidu that his party's ties with the UF would be more stable than in the past and serve the interests of all secular groups.
The Pioneer
FINANCE BILL IN TROUBLE

The passage of the Finance Bill appeared uncertain. Both the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Left parties expressed reservations on completing the economic agenda of a defeated government. With this, it was apparent that a consensus reached on the passage of the Finance Bill at an all-party meeting before the government lost the confidence vote, was no longer valid. In a letter to the President, the BJP asserted that it would not be fair if the special session became another device to complete the economic agenda of a defeated government. A Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader also said he was not happy with the idea from the beginning.
The Economic Times
CREDIT DELIVERY SYSTEM MADE MORE FLEXIBLE

The monetary and credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) broke the shackles on lenders and borrowers alike, razed the walls between different market segments, allowed interest rates to come into their own and opened the floodgates for capital movement between providers and users. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) cut the term deposit rate, increased lendable resources of banks by 33.25 billion rupees and gave them complete freedom to determine credit limits of borrowers.
MARKET UP MARGINALLY FOLLOWING ANNOUNCEMENTS

The lingering political instability and a pragmatic six-month monetary policy pulled the stock market in the opposite direction. The stock market edged up marginally following the central bank's announcements. Late evening kerb dealings found pivotals perked up on speculative buying enquiries. The market opened on a firm note on expectations of a solution to the political uncertainty in the wake of indications of a change in the United Front coalition's leadership.
LENDING, DEPOSIT RATES START FALLING

The prime lending rates (PLR) of banks began their descent hours after the announcement of the credit policy. Many state-owned banks indicated their intent to cut their PLRs to 14 percent. Leading finacial institution sources said their managements would meet soon to review the situation.
IOBL KICKSTARTS FIRST TITANIUM GREASE COMPLEX

Indian Oil Blending (IOBL) commissioned its 64 million rupee titanium complex grease plant, the first of its kind in the world, in New Bombay. The plant has a capacity of 3,000 tonne per annum. The indigenously developed grease was a technological breakthrough and would be marketed as Servo Titex HT. IOBL is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the state owned Indian Oil Corporation. Titanium complex grease was expected to emerge as a replacement for conventional lithium, aluminium and clay based greases. The product has already recieved patents in various countries.
Financial Express
FOREIGN EXCHANGE MARKET MAY TURN SPECULATIVE

The central bank's decision to permit corporates to book forward contracts beyond six months without an underlying trade transaction may trigger speculative activities by exporters. The move to allow banks to offer rupee-foreign exchange swaps and the general permission given to banks to run a swap-book would also give the derivatives market a big fillip. Senior bankers felt many corpoorates may now overstate their future receivables in dollars to bankers who would book forward cover beyond six months for them.
OIL REFINERIES CAN SET UP POWER PROJECTS

Oil refineries would be permitted to enter power generation for sale of surplus electricty to state grids. However, these power plants would have to be based on petroleum residues such as heavy petroleum stock (HPS) and vaccum residue (VR). The Power Ministry consented to the Petroleum Ministry's proposal seeking permission for state-owned oil refiners to set up power projects using liquid fuels.
ONGC IN JOINT VENTURE TO EXPLOIT OILFIELD

The board of the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) approved a 50:50 joint venture with a multinational oil company for exploiting the reserves of the Neelam Oilfield on the Bombay offshore. The joint venture was expected to help ONGC manage its resources better.
Business Standard
POLICY TO FAVOUR DEBT SEGMENT

Market circles were of the view that the credit policy announcements would largely favour the debt segment of the capital market rather than equities. The removal of the five percent cap in investments in bonds, debentures and preference shares would indirectly mean that banks could now route the entire allocation of incremental deposits into equities.
ONE YEAR MONEY AT 10 PERCENT

As a fallout of the scrapping of the cash reserve ratio and the statutory liquidity ratio on inter-bank deposits, the rate on six month was quoted at nine percent and one year money was priced at 10 percent. Barely three hours after the slack season credit policy was announced, the rupee climbed to 35.795, its strongest position so far this year, before closing at 35.815/35.825.
NATIONAL PROGRAMME ON GAS HYDRATES TO BE LAUNCHED

The Petroleum Ministry is planning to launch a national programme on gas hydrates in collaboration with the United States and Japan to exploit gas reserves. The petroleum and natural gas secretary said the programme would be financed by the Oil Industry Development Bank. The ministry has prepared a draft bill for setting up the gas regulatory agency and strengthening of the directorate-general of hydrocarbons (DGH).
INDIA PLANS TO IMPORT ELECTRICITY FROM PAKISTAN

India, Pakistan and Bangladesh will form a confederation for supply of electricity, with the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank playing the mediator. India planned to import 3,000 megawatts from Pakistan over 15 months, with the first supply of 1,000 megawatts scheduled in a couple of months. The country would export power to Bangladesh from two points in West Bengal and Meghalaya, while Bangladesh would supply power to Tripura. The power grids of the three countries would not be directly linked, owing to technical problems.
COKE FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT PROPOSAL PUT ON HOLD

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) deferred a fresh investment proposal by Coca-Cola South Asia Holdings, which sought to capitalise the multinational's two proposed 100 percent bottling subsidiaries in the country. The proposal was to set up 12.53 billion rupees as the equity share capital of Coca-Cola's two wholly-owned bottling subsidiaries in phases. A final decision was deferred as FIPB was yet to receive the necessary comments from the Food Processing Ministry.
